memos.headline: S01 Stands Alone as Relative Strength Leader; S03, S10, S06 in Oversold Free-Fall
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape across this universe as of March 7. S01 is the clear standout — trading just 2.1% off its 52-week high, above both its 50d and 200d means, with RSI at 63 and the strongest 4-week (+9.2%) and 12-week (+6.5%) relative strength vs SPY. S08 and S09 are holding near their 50d averages with neutral RSI readings, making them range-bound names I'd watch but not chase. On the downside, S03 (RSI 29.8, -16.6% over 4 weeks), S10 (RSI 37.8, -20.9% over 12 weeks, -14.5% below 50d), and S06 (RSI 30.3, -12.5% over 4 weeks) are in clear downtrends with no sign of stabilization — catching these knives is premature until we see RSI divergences or reclaims of the 50d mean. I have highest conviction in S01 long and S10 avoid; the middle of the pack requires patience.

views.note: Near 52w highs, above both moving averages, RSI 63, best relative strength in the universe — would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~167).
Flat at the 50d mean with +5.3% cushion above 200d and +7.5% 4w relative strength vs SPY; low-volatility leader but needs a breakout above 258 (52w high area) for higher conviction.
Sitting right on its 50d mean with a neutral RSI of 49.6 and modest positive relative strength; below the 200d mean by 4.6% keeps me from getting constructive — would turn long above 116.
Down 24.6% from highs, 14.5% below 50d, RSI 37.8, worst 12w relative strength at -15.6% vs SPY — no reason to step in until price reclaims the 50d mean (~132).
RSI 29.8 is the lowest in the universe, -16.6% over 4 weeks, 11.2% below 50d — textbook breakdown; would reconsider only on a weekly close back above 220.
RSI 30.3 with an 8.5% drop in just one week and -12.5% over 4 weeks; still above 200d mean (+6.7%) which could offer support near 227, but trend is clearly broken.
Trading 5.8% below 50d and 7.5% below 200d with RSI 39.5 and -15.9% drawdown — sustained downtrend with negative 12w relative strength of -6.1%; needs to reclaim 415 area.
Deepest 26w drawdown at -16.2% and 9.5% below 200d, but last week's +3.9% bounce and RSI near 48 suggest possible basing; too early to call a turn — watching 510 as confirmation.
Bounced +2.1% last week but still 7.8% below 50d with RSI 40.5; positive 12w relative strength (+4.8%) is a silver lining — would get constructive on a move back above 188.
Mid-range RSI 49.1, 3.5% below 50d, 16% off highs — no clear edge either way; a close above 365 (50d area) would tilt me long.

memos.headline: S10's 56% Net Margin and 78% Revenue Growth Stand Out; S02 and S09 Show Earnings-Power Weakness
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in S10, which posted $39.3B in revenue (+77.9% YoY) with a 56.2% net margin and only $8.5B in total debt—an extraordinary combination of growth, profitability, and balance-sheet strength. S05 and S04 also impress with net margins of 27.5% and 34.6% respectively, double-digit revenue growth, and manageable leverage. On the other end, S02 at a 5.5% net margin on $100.8B revenue with $76.9B in debt and only +1.6% net income growth is a name I cannot get comfortable with, and S09's -1.1% revenue decline paired with a thin 9.1% margin signals cash-flow compression risk. S03's 88.3% net income jump is eye-catching, but the 10.7% margin on $187.8B revenue and $58B debt means the earnings recovery needs to prove durability before I'd add exposure. A margin reversal in S10 below 40% or a deceleration in revenue growth below 30% would change my conviction there.

views.note: 56.2% net margin, 77.9% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt ($8.5B) represent best-in-class earnings power in this universe.
27.5% net margin with 11.8% revenue growth and low debt ($14.8B) signals durable, high-quality earnings.
34.6% net margin and 12.3% revenue growth are strong, though $45B in debt warrants monitoring.
32.7% margin and 50.5% NI growth are attractive, but $401B total debt (financial-sector leverage) limits conviction.
88.3% NI growth is impressive but off a low base; 10.7% margin on $188B revenue needs to prove sustainability.
29.2% margin is solid but revenue growth of only 4% YoY on $124B is decelerating; need to see re-acceleration.
21.2% margin and 33.5% NI growth are decent, but only 2.1% revenue growth and $25B debt on $22B revenue give me pause.
Revenue declined 5% YoY to $16.2B with $31.7B in debt—leverage is nearly 2x revenue, and top-line shrinkage is a red flag.
Revenue down 1.1% YoY, 9.1% net margin, and $36.8B debt point to weak and potentially compressing cash-flow generation.
5.5% net margin on $100.8B revenue with $76.9B debt and only 1.6% NI growth is insufficient earnings power for the risk.

memos.headline: Fed Pausing at 4.50% With Sticky 3% CPI – Favor Staples and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound sits at 4.50%, down 100bp over 12 months but unchanged since the last 25bp cut three months ago, while CPI is running at 3.0% YoY—well above the 2% target. The labor market remains resilient with unemployment at 4.0%, down 10bp over three months, giving the Fed no urgency to ease further. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+77bp YoY to +0.33pp), which is constructive for bank net interest margins but signals the market is pricing in persistent inflation and higher-for-longer rates. I have conviction that this pause-with-sticky-inflation regime favors banks and defensive staples while creating headwinds for long-duration growth names; a CPI print falling below 2.5% or unemployment rising above 4.3% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing.

views.note: Banks benefit from a steepening curve (+0.33pp 10y-2y spread) and a pause regime that keeps short rates elevated, supporting NIM expansion.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a higher-for-longer rate environment with 3% CPI supporting pricing power.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds as 10y yields remain elevated at 4.32% and the Fed pause removes near-term easing catalysts.
High-multiple tech/growth names are vulnerable to sustained 4.3%+ long rates with no imminent rate relief.
Cyclicals face mixed signals: solid labor market supports demand but sticky inflation and elevated rates cap upside.
Energy is a hedge against persistent inflation but lacks a clear macro catalyst in a pause regime with stable unemployment.

memos.headline: Broad Negative Earnings-Reaction Tone Across Universe; S01 and S06 Stand Out as Positive Outliers
memos.body: I reviewed post-earnings price reactions and filing activity across the universe through 2025-03-07. The dominant pattern is sharply negative sentiment: S10 dropped -8.5%, S05 -7.3%, S04 -6.2%, S02 -6.0%, S07 -4.6%, S03 -4.1%, and S09 -2.5% on their respective results filings. The only two names that bucked this trend are S01 (+1.9% on Q2 FY25 results) and S06 (+2.0% on Jan 15 results), both of which also showed constructive follow-on filing activity (dividend declaration for S01, multiple governance and Reg FD filings for S06). Given that the negative reactions are now 4-6 weeks old, much of the bad news is likely priced, but I have higher conviction in the positive-tone outliers as potential longs and would avoid the deepest negative-reaction names where sentiment may still be deteriorating.

views.note: Only name with a positive earnings reaction (+1.9%) plus a quarterly dividend declaration, signaling constructive tone.
Positive +2.0% earnings reaction and heavy filing cadence (governance, Reg FD, bylaws) suggest active corporate narrative without negative market read.
Most severe negative reaction in the universe at -8.5% on Feb 26 results; recency of the selloff means sentiment likely still impaired.
Sharp -7.3% post-earnings drop on Feb 4 signals deeply negative tone that may not yet be fully washed out.
-6.2% earnings reaction combined with a director departure filing suggests negative narrative momentum.
-6.0% earnings reaction on Jan 16 is now aged enough that some recovery is possible, but no positive catalysts visible.
Mild -0.7% earnings reaction is essentially flat; no strong sentiment signal in either direction.
-2.5% post-earnings move is moderate; tone is mildly negative but not extreme enough for a strong directional call.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surge Signals Structural Geopolitical Risk Across the Universe
memos.body: I am seeing an extraordinary spike in policy uncertainty: the EPU index hit 726.26 on March 6, nearly doubling over one month (+95%) and up 86% over three months, while the VIX has surged to 24.87 (+95% over 3m). This is not a one-quarter event—the magnitude and persistence of the move suggest a structural shift in the policy environment, likely driven by escalating trade/tariff actions, sanctions regimes, or export-control tightening. Notably, WTI crude has fallen 6.1% over the past month to $66.62/bbl, which is unusual alongside rising geopolitical stress and may reflect demand-destruction fears or supply-side policy shifts. High-yield spreads have widened 33bp over one month to 2.99%, confirming that credit markets are beginning to price policy tail risk. Without specific 8-K content beyond filing categories, I cannot differentiate company-level geopolitical exposure with high confidence, but the macro backdrop warrants broad caution, particularly for names with supply-chain concentration or China/energy policy sensitivity.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in six weeks suggest active corporate developments, but without detail on geopolitical exposure I stay neutral amid elevated policy uncertainty.
Two Reg FD filings in January indicate proactive investor communication, but the macro policy uncertainty backdrop at 726 EPU keeps me sidelined until clarity emerges.
With VIX near 25 and EPU almost doubled in a month, the risk-reward for names without clear geopolitical hedges is poor; a single 8-K gives me no offsetting comfort.
Elevated policy uncertainty and widening HY spreads (+33bp in one month) argue against risk-taking in names where I lack visibility on sanctions or export-control exposure.
Reg FD filing in late January is stale; the falling oil price (-6.1% 1m) could be a tailwind or headwind depending on sector, so I hold neutral with low conviction.
Single Reg FD disclosure provides minimal signal; I would need clarity on tariff or supply-chain exposure before taking a directional view given the current EPU spike.

We concentrate in S01 (strongest technicals and positive sentiment), add modest positions in S08 (low-vol range leader) and S06 (curve steepening beneficiary despite recent weakness), and keep a small allocation to S04 (defensive staples) while holding ~45% cash as a buffer against geopolitical tail risk.

Technical and Sentiment analysts both flag it as the top long. Fundamentals are middling and macro analyst flags duration headwinds, so we size just below max.
plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below the 50-day mean (~167, roughly -5%) would negate the relative-strength thesis and trigger an exit.

Fundamentals show a solid 29.2% margin though growth is decelerating. A safe place to park capital while waiting for clarity. Technical analyst is mildly constructive.
plans.changes_my_mind: A break below the 200d mean (roughly 227, ~5% below current) or a VIX spike above 30 with no corresponding bounce would prompt an exit.

plans.rationale: Macro analyst's top pick as a steepening-curve beneficiary (10y-2y +0.33pp) with positive earnings sentiment (+2.0% reaction). However, technicals are ugly (RSI 30.3, -8.5% last week), creating analyst conflict. We size down meaningfully and use a wider stop to respect the oversold bounce potential near the 200d (~227).
plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below 227 (200d support area) would confirm the breakdown and invalidate the mean-reversion thesis.

However, technicals are negative (RSI 39.5, below both MAs) and sentiment was poor (-6.2% earnings reaction plus director departure). Sized small due to conflicting signals.
